inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Risk-free ~4.3% (10y UST) + 5.0% ERP x beta ~1.05 = cost of equity ~9.5%; pre-tax cost of debt ~5.5% (4.5% after tax); market-value weights ~67% equity / 33% net debt -> ~7.9%, rounded to 8.0%. One WACC for all three scenarios: risk is charged in the scenario paths and weights, not a second time in the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP operating leases (~$290m liability): rent is already inside EBITDA, so lease liabilities are NOT added to net debt. One treatment.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (operating pharma company; routing table row 'operating company'; no memory entry - first valuation). 10-year horizon. KEY JUDGMENT - ebitda_margin_path is NOT company 'adjusted EBITDA' margin (30.4% on FY2026 guidance of $4.45-4.55bn). Viatris' adjusted EBITDA has excluded ~$0.8-1.1bn a year of cash restructuring, remediation, litigation, divestiture and working-capital cost in every year since the 2020 combination. Backing cash EBITDA out of the cash-flow statement (OCF + cash interest + est. cash taxes) gives ~28% of revenue in FY2023, ~23% in FY2024, ~24% in FY2025 and ~21-23% in FY2026E, against adjusted margins of 33/32/29/30%. The path here is that all-in cash margin (before SBC), so the chronic 'special items' and the inventory build are charged in the flows; wc_capture is therefore 0. da_pct_path is DEPRECIATION only (~2.6% of revenue): the ~$2.3bn/yr of acquired-intangible amortisation is a non-cash purchase-accounting charge excluded from the tax base here, and cash_tax_rate_path is set near the company's adjusted effective rate on that base (unlevered - no interest shield). capex_pct_path = PP&E capex (~2.4%, guidance $325-400m) plus recurring payments for product rights and IPR&D (~0.6%). fy0 is FY2026E at the guidance midpoint ($14.7-14.9bn), with the 30 Sep 2026 balance sheet; Q4-2026 free cash flow (~$0.3-0.4bn) is not credited, a small conservatism. PACIRA: the ~$1.65bn cash tender (expires 16 Nov 2026, close expected end-Nov) is treated as value-neutral - neither the purchase price nor Pacira's flows are in the model, and guidance excludes it. On close, the next update must add the cash paid, Pacira's own debt/cash and its revenue/EBITDA. The Biocon stake ($815m) was fully monetised by 14 Jul 2026 and is already in cash. Contingent consideration ($440.8m fair value, mostly Idorsia milestones) is NOT deducted because the pipeline revenue it would be paid against is not in the base path (matching rule). After-hours: none; price is a regular close near the 52-week high.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (-11.3% 3yr, -8.5% 5yr) reflects $3.8bn of goodwill impairments and divestiture losses, not operating shrinkage; it diverges >30% from revenue. EPS CAGRs are undefined (GAAP losses in FY2020, FY2021, FY2024, FY2025). All 5-year figures start at FY2020, which held only six weeks of Upjohn, and are merger-distorted.

Owner FCF fell slightly faster than reported FCF (-10.9% vs -9.3%). Revenue decline is mostly divestitures (biosimilars, OTC, women's health, API) plus base erosion and the Indore import alert.

scenario_narratives.base: Revenue holds roughly flat in nominal terms: Greater China (+19% over nine months) and ~$450m a year of new-product revenue offset continued erosion in commoditised generics, JANZ and the legacy brands. The $600-700m EWSR savings arrive over 2026-2028 but roughly a third is consumed by price erosion and reinvestment, and the chronic stream of 'special' cash costs shrinks without disappearing once the $650-750m restructuring cash is spent. All-in cash EBITDA margin rises from ~23% to 26.5% - still four points below what the company calls adjusted EBITDA. Terminal growth 0.5%; the 12x cap binds over Gordon (13.4x).
scenario_narratives.bull: The turnaround is real: EWSR savings drop through, Indore and Nashik supply normalises, lifecycle management holds the Lipitor/Norvasc/EpiPen franchises, China keeps compounding and the innovative pipeline (selatogrel, cenerimod, pitolisant in Japan) plus bolt-ons such as Pacira add branded growth. Revenue grows 1.5-2.5% and the special-item drag falls to ~2% of revenue, taking the cash margin to 29%.
scenario_narratives.bear: Generic price deflation, US and European drug-pricing reform and tariffs on an India/China-weighted supply chain outrun the savings; another plant event follows Indore and Nashik; litigation (EpiPen antitrust, generic price-fixing MDL, the Pfizer opioid cost-sharing dispute) keeps consuming cash. Revenue shrinks ~2% a year, the cash margin never gets above 22.5% and decays to 21%, and the business is capitalised as a run-off portfolio (-1% terminal growth, 9x cap) against $11.5bn of net debt.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from 15% to 25%: six years of revenue and cash-flow decline, two India plant failures in two years, live litigation and net debt of ~2.6x adjusted EBITDA make the downside a continuation of the record, not a tail. Base 50%: it is what FY2026 guidance and the EWSR plan describe after a haircut for the company's history of recurring special items. Bull cut from 35% to 25%: it needs savings delivery, supply normalisation, brand durability and pipeline success to all happen together.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Viatris is valued on the cash it actually produces, not on adjusted EBITDA. The company's adjusted measures have excluded roughly a billion dollars a year of cash cost for six straight years; this model charges that cost in the flows and lets it shrink only partly. On that basis the equity is a leveraged claim on a flat-to-eroding portfolio, and value per share is highly sensitive to the cash margin because $11.5bn of net debt sits ahead of it.
key_risks_to_valuation: Leverage: every 1pp of sustained cash EBITDA margin moves equity value by roughly $1.2-1.5 per share
Whether 'special items' really decline after the EWSR - the base case assumes they fall from ~7% to ~4% of revenue
Pacira is treated as value-neutral at a 45% premium; overpayment or integration failure is not in the numbers, nor is upside from EXPAREL/ZILRETTA
Cash tax base is an approximation (depreciation-only D&A at the adjusted effective rate); Pillar Two or loss of amortisation deductions would raise it
Litigation beyond the $309m accrued (EpiPen, generic price-fixing MDL, Pfizer opioid indemnity dispute) is unquantified
Pipeline (selatogrel, cenerimod) is excluded from base flows along with its $441m contingent consideration
